newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-NEW TOUR COMMISSIONER MENZ IS A MAN IN A HURRY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NEW TOUR COMMISSIONER MENZ IS A MAN IN A HURRY.

text.p: New Southern African PGA tour commissioner Arnold Mentz is a man in a hurry.
A former career diplomat with the South African government, Mentz took over as tour commissioner in December last year.
Already he has seen enough to call for changes, including staging more tournaments in November and December and substantially increasing prize money.
"We must try to copy what the Nordic countries have achieved over the past decade," he said in an interview.
"Just look at how many of their players are performing successfully all over the world and how many are challenging to Ryder Cup places.
"We must learn from the U.S. tour, from Europe, Japan and from Australia but the end result should have a South African identity on it."
Mentz said the tour should also concentrate on "getting the prize money right" to attract top players.
"Our tour is certainly moving in the right direction and players like Ernie Els, Nick Price and Mark McNulty are all well established names at the very highest level," he said.

"Yet our tour has always been regarded as a stepping-stone tour for the young players to cut their teeth and to get some exposure. For example, the likes of Americans Corey Pavin, John Daly and Tommy Tolles all played here in their earlier years.
"We have all the ingredients for professional golf here in South Africa, and with even greater depth here, so the sky should be the limit."
The 49-year-old, a skilled amateur golfer, inherited a tour which had increased its sponsorship substantially over the previous three years.

"It is important that the players feel their needs and requirements are being taken care of and that the association is arranging their business affairs. We have to work as a team with both the players and the sponsors to put golf back where it should be -- at number one," Mentz said.
"And if the players and sponsors get the best out of it, then golf will be the winner as well."

Mentz said he was satisfied with a 1996-97 tour which featured three European co-sanctioned tournaments, including a South African Open at Glendower narrowly won by Fiji's Vijay Singh from the strongest field ever assembled for the event.

"That was a great finish with Vijay beating Nick Price by a single shot but I doubt if we'll increase the number of co-sanctioned events, this is our tour and all additional tournaments must be South African events. If the prize money is right, then the top foreign players would certainly have a look at it."
Mentz stressed the tour should take better advantage of the good weather during November and December.

"We need to increase the number of events on the summer part of the tour, with three or four being staged in the Cape. From a climatic point of view, we shold start our tour in the Cape before Christmas, then move on to Gauteng and Swaziland before finishing in Natal."
